paperInfo.subject: Social Science
paperInfo.paperName: Grade 7 Social Science — Paper 1 (Practice Set B - Heritage, RME & Social Studies)

questions.questionText: To which mountain did Moses go up to receive the Ten Commandments from God?
questions.explanation: Moses received the Ten Commandments from God on Mount Sinai, as recorded in the book of Exodus.

questions.questionText: The Bible teaches that we should forgive others because

options.text: God has forgiven us and expects us to forgive others too.

questions.explanation: A central Christian teaching is that believers should forgive others just as God has forgiven them.

questions.questionText: The Bible teaches that Jesus rose from the dead on the
questions.explanation: Christian teaching holds that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion and burial.

questions.questionText: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" Who said these words about Jesus?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said these words when he saw Jesus approaching, as recorded in the Gospel of John.

questions.questionText: Most religions found in Zimbabwe agree that we must

options.text: honour and care for our parents and elders.
fast during a specific month only.

questions.explanation: Respect and care for parents/elders is a value shared broadly across the different religious and cultural traditions practised in Zimbabwe.

questions.questionText: Among the following pairs of Jesus' disciples, who were brothers?
questions.explanation: James and John, sons of Zebedee, were brothers among Jesus' twelve disciples.

questions.questionText: Which Roman governor questioned Jesus and eventually allowed him to be crucified?
questions.explanation: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor who questioned Jesus and ultimately handed him over to be crucified.

questions.questionText: What does the parable of the Good Samaritan teach us?

options.text: Showing kindness/love to everyone, even strangers

questions.explanation: The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches that we should show kindness and compassion to anyone in need, regardless of who they are.

questions.questionText: African Traditional Religion teaches that

options.text: only ancestors should be worshipped, and God is not important.
ancestors have no influence on the living.
ancestors can act as intermediaries between the living and God.
there are many different gods, one for each family.

questions.explanation: A central belief in African Traditional Religion is that ancestral spirits (vadzimu/abezimu) can intercede or communicate between the living and the Supreme Being/God.

questions.questionText: Child neglect and abandonment would be reduced if people believed that

options.text: children are a burden on the family.
the government alone is responsible for children.
only wealthy families should raise children.
every child's life has value and deserves love and care.

questions.explanation: The belief that every child's life has inherent value and deserves love and care is what discourages neglect or abandonment.

questions.questionText: A bira/umbuyiso ceremony is held by African Traditional Religion followers mainly to

options.text: communicate with and honour the ancestral spirits.
mark the start of the farming season only.

questions.explanation: A bira (or umbuyiso in Ndebele culture) is a traditional ceremony held to communicate with, honour and appease the ancestral spirits.

questions.questionText: David showed loyalty to his friend Jonathan by

options.text: caring for Jonathan's son Mephibosheth after Jonathan's death.

questions.explanation: David honoured his covenant of friendship with Jonathan by showing kindness to Jonathan's disabled son, Mephibosheth, after Jonathan died.

questions.questionText: A good leader is one who

options.text: serves and leads by good example.

questions.explanation: A good leader serves their followers and leads by setting a positive example, rather than ruling through fear or self-enrichment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following religions celebrates the festival of Eid al-Fitr?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is an Islamic festival marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: The Second Chimurenga/Umvukela is generally considered to have begun with the Battle of
questions.explanation: The Battle of Chinhoyi in April 1966 is widely regarded as marking the start of the Second Chimurenga/Umvukela.

questions.questionText: During the ceasefire period leading to Zimbabwe's independence, freedom fighters gathered at designated
questions.explanation: Freedom fighters gathered at designated Assembly Points during the ceasefire period ahead of the 1980 elections.

questions.questionText: The San people traditionally used _______ to store and carry water.
questions.explanation: The San (Bushmen) traditionally used hollowed-out ostrich egg shells as portable water containers, especially in dry desert regions.

questions.questionText: Which Ndebele king signed the Rudd Concession in 1888?
questions.explanation: King Lobengula signed the Rudd Concession in 1888, granting mining rights to agents of Cecil Rhodes.

questions.questionText: Which group is generally credited with building the Great Zimbabwe Ruins?

options.text: The Shona (ancestors of the Shona, likely the Gokomere/Karanga peoples)

questions.explanation: Archaeological and historical evidence generally credits the ancestors of the Shona people (the Karanga/Gokomere builders) with constructing the Great Zimbabwe Ruins between roughly the 11th and 15th centuries.

questions.questionText: People who build homes on land without legal permission are called
questions.explanation: Squatters are people who occupy and build on land without legal ownership or permission.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a root crop?
questions.explanation: A sweet potato is a root crop - the edible part grows underground as a swollen root, unlike cabbage (leaf), tomato (fruit) or pea (seed/pod).

questions.questionText: _______ is a nutrient found mainly in body-building foods.
questions.explanation: Protein is the main nutrient in body-building foods, needed for growth and repair of body tissues.

questions.questionText: On a map of Zimbabwe, a town marked in the far northwest, near the Zambezi River and Zambia's border, close to a major hydro-electric dam, is most likely to be
questions.explanation: Victoria Falls is located in the far northwest of Zimbabwe, on the Zambezi River near the Zambian border, close to major hydro-electric power generation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a pair of disease vectors (animals that spread disease)?
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes (which spread malaria) and tsetse flies (which spread sleeping sickness) are both disease vectors - animals that transmit disease-causing organisms.

questions.questionText: A rondavel (traditional round hut) is typically built using
questions.explanation: A traditional rondavel is typically built with mud (or brick) walls and a thatched grass roof.

questions.questionText: What type of buildings would you expect to find mostly in a residential area?
questions.explanation: A residential area is mainly made up of houses/homes where people live, unlike an industrial area which has factories and warehouses.

questions.questionText: Very tall multi-storey buildings commonly found in a city centre are called
questions.explanation: Very tall multi-storey buildings, especially common in city centres, are called skyscrapers.

questions.questionText: When there is not enough money circulating in an economy, leading to reduced spending and slower economic activity, this is called
questions.explanation: Deflation refers to a general fall in prices/reduced money circulation in an economy, often linked to reduced spending and slower economic activity.

questions.questionText: Large wild animals such as elephants and lions would most likely be found in a Zimbabwean
questions.explanation: National parks (such as Hwange or Mana Pools) are protected areas set aside for wildlife such as elephants and lions to live undisturbed.

questions.questionText: Exchanging goods directly for other goods, without using money, is called
questions.explanation: Barter trade is the direct exchange of goods or services for other goods or services, without using money.

questions.questionText: Ice is water in what state?
questions.explanation: Ice is the solid state of water, formed when water freezes at or below 0 degrees Celsius.

questions.questionText: The process in which water changes from a liquid to a gas (vapour) is called
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process by which liquid water changes into water vapour (gas), usually due to heating.

questions.questionText: In a typical flower, the colourful part that attracts insects for pollination is called the
questions.explanation: The petal is the often brightly coloured part of a flower that helps attract insects and other pollinators.

questions.questionText: You can help stop a veld fire from spreading by
questions.explanation: Firebreaks (cleared strips of land without vegetation) help stop the spread of veld fires by removing fuel the fire needs to keep burning.

questions.questionText: The gradual breaking down of rocks into smaller particles to eventually form soil is called
questions.explanation: Weathering is the process by which rocks are gradually broken down (by water, temperature changes, plant roots, etc.) into smaller particles that eventually form soil.

questions.questionText: Animals that feed mainly on grass close to the ground are called
questions.explanation: Grazers (such as zebra and cattle) feed mainly on grass close to the ground, while browsers (such as giraffes and kudu) feed on leaves and shoots from trees and shrubs.

questions.questionText: What sweet, thick by-product do we get from processing sugarcane, sometimes used to feed cattle?
questions.explanation: Molasses is a thick, sweet by-product of sugar processing from sugarcane, and is commonly used as a supplement to feed cattle.

questions.questionText: The best way to avoid sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) is to

options.text: practise safe sex, including abstinence or correct condom use.

questions.explanation: STDs are spread mainly through sexual contact, so abstinence or correctly using protection (such as condoms) are the most effective ways to avoid them.

questions.questionText: Which weather station instrument is used to measure the amount of rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge is the instrument specifically used to measure and collect the amount of rainfall at a weather station.

questions.questionText: Changing the type of crop grown on the same piece of land each season, to help maintain soil fertility, is called
questions.explanation: Crop rotation is the practice of changing the type of crop grown on a piece of land from season to season, helping to maintain soil fertility and reduce pest/disease build-up.

questions.questionText: Electricity generated from the energy of falling or flowing water is called
questions.explanation: Hydro-electric power (or hydro power) is electricity generated using the energy of falling or fast-flowing water, such as at Kariba Dam.

questions.questionText: The joining of a male sex cell (sperm) and a female sex cell (egg) is called
questions.explanation: Fertilisation is the specific term for the joining/fusion of a male sex cell and a female sex cell to form a new life.

questions.questionText: The rotation of the Earth on its own axis causes
questions.explanation: The Earth's rotation on its own axis (taking about 24 hours) causes the cycle of day and night, as different parts face towards or away from the sun.

questions.questionText: It is dangerous to keep swimming when a thunderstorm approaches mainly because

options.text: water is a good conductor and can attract or conduct lightning strikes.
swimming pools attract more insects during storms.

questions.explanation: Water is a good conductor of electricity, so it can attract or conduct lightning strikes, making swimming during a thunderstorm dangerous.

questions.questionText: Rainfall is measured in which unit?
questions.explanation: Rainfall is measured in millimetres (mm), representing the depth of water that would collect on a flat surface.

questions.questionText: What is the correct recipe for making an Oral Rehydration Solution (Sugar-Salt Solution) at home?

options.text: 750ml of clean water, equal amounts of sugar and salt.
750ml of clean water, 6 teaspoons of salt, and 1/2 teaspoon of sugar.
750ml of clean water, 6 tablespoons of sugar, and 1/2 tablespoon of salt.
750ml of clean water, 6 teaspoons of sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt.

questions.explanation: The standard home-made Sugar-Salt Solution (SSS) for treating dehydration is 750ml (about a large bottle) of clean water, 6 level teaspoons of sugar, and 1/2 a level teaspoon of salt.

questions.questionText: From which of the following foods do we mainly get carbohydrates?
questions.explanation: Sadza (made from maize meal) and bread are both starchy, energy-giving foods that are rich sources of carbohydrates.

questions.questionText: After using the toilet, you should always

options.text: wipe your hands on your clothes.
wash your hands thoroughly with clean water and soap.
use the same water for drinking.

questions.explanation: Washing hands thoroughly with clean water and soap after using the toilet is essential to prevent the spread of germs and disease.

questions.questionText: Eggs can be boiled, fried or
questions.explanation: Scrambling is a common way of cooking eggs, alongside boiling and frying.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: Tinned/canned foods remain safe to eat forever, even after opening.
Undercooked meat is always safe to eat.
Eating any amount of red meat always causes malnutrition.
Overcooking vegetables for too long can destroy some of their nutrients.

questions.explanation: Overcooking, especially vegetables, can break down and destroy heat-sensitive nutrients such as vitamin C, reducing the food's nutritional value.

questions.questionText: Which site is famous for its ancient stone walls and is an important heritage site in Zimbabwe?
questions.explanation: Great Zimbabwe is a major archaeological and cultural heritage site.

questions.questionText: Which material was commonly used by traditional builders to make strong walls in Great Zimbabwe?
questions.explanation: Granite blocks were used in the dry-stone construction.

questions.questionText: Why should communities protect cultural heritage sites?

options.text: To prevent children from learning history
To replace old buildings with shops

questions.explanation: Heritage sites help preserve history, culture and identity.

questions.questionText: Which activity best demonstrates respect for a community's cultural heritage?
questions.explanation: Protecting heritage ensures it is available for future generations.

questions.questionText: What is an artefact?

options.text: An object made or used by people in the past

questions.explanation: Artefacts are objects that provide evidence about past human life.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps pass indigenous knowledge from one generation to another?
questions.explanation: Oral storytelling is an important way of transmitting knowledge.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a tangible form of cultural heritage?
questions.explanation: A traditional building is a physical heritage resource.

questions.questionText: Which item is most closely associated with traditional music?
questions.explanation: Drums are widely used in traditional music and ceremonies.

questions.questionText: Why are traditional ceremonies important to communities?

options.text: They can strengthen identity and social bonds

questions.explanation: Ceremonies can reinforce identity, values and community relationships.

questions.questionText: Which action is most appropriate when visiting a heritage monument?

options.text: Follow the site's rules and avoid damaging it

questions.explanation: Following rules protects the monument.

questions.questionText: A family keeps photographs, letters and objects belonging to grandparents. These items can help children to:
questions.explanation: Family records provide evidence about previous generations.

questions.questionText: Which person is most likely to preserve oral history in a community?

options.text: An elder who remembers past events

questions.explanation: Elders often carry memories and stories of community history.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a museum?

options.text: To preserve and display objects of historical or cultural value

questions.explanation: Museums preserve and display collections for learning.

questions.questionText: Which behaviour shows respect for another community's culture?

options.text: Learning about it without insulting its practices

questions.explanation: Respectful learning promotes understanding and cooperation.

questions.questionText: Why should children learn local history?

options.text: It helps them understand their community and identity
It removes the need for citizenship

questions.explanation: Local history connects learners with their community and heritage.

questions.questionText: Which household practice best promotes cooperation among family members?

options.text: Giving all work to one person

questions.explanation: Sharing suitable duties promotes teamwork.

questions.questionText: Why is it important to listen when another person is speaking?

options.text: It shows respect and helps communication
It makes people unable to cooperate

questions.explanation: Listening helps people understand one another.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of a community service?
questions.explanation: Community service involves useful work for the common good.

questions.questionText: A good friend is most likely to:

options.text: Refuse to help in every situation

questions.explanation: A good friend supports others responsibly.

questions.questionText: Which action can help resolve a disagreement peacefully?
questions.explanation: Calm discussion allows people to seek a fair solution.

questions.questionText: Why should boys and girls be given equal opportunities to learn?

options.text: Both can develop their abilities and contribute to society

questions.explanation: Equal educational opportunity supports fairness and development.

questions.questionText: Which behaviour shows responsibility at home?

options.text: Ignoring younger children who need help

questions.explanation: Responsibility includes carrying out agreed duties.

questions.questionText: What is one benefit of working together in a community?

options.text: Problems can be solved using shared effort

questions.explanation: Cooperation combines skills and effort.

questions.questionText: Which person is usually responsible for helping a child learn acceptable behaviour at home?
questions.explanation: Parents and guardians play an important role in guidance and socialisation.

questions.questionText: Why should family members respect one another's belongings?

options.text: It protects trust and reduces conflict

questions.explanation: Respect for property supports trust and peaceful relationships.

questions.questionText: Which action is most helpful when a neighbour is facing a temporary problem?
questions.explanation: Reasonable assistance strengthens community support.

questions.questionText: A community meeting is most useful when residents want to:

options.text: Discuss shared problems and possible solutions

questions.explanation: Meetings allow communities to identify issues and agree on action.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of fair sharing?

options.text: Giving every task to the youngest child
Allowing one person to take everything
Dividing work according to ability and agreed responsibilities

questions.explanation: Fair sharing considers responsibilities and circumstances.

questions.questionText: Why is keeping promises important?
questions.explanation: Keeping promises helps others rely on us.

questions.questionText: Which action can strengthen unity in a community?

options.text: Respecting differences while working toward common goals

questions.explanation: Respectful cooperation strengthens unity.

questions.questionText: Which quality is commonly associated with a trustworthy person?
questions.explanation: Honesty helps people trust one another.

questions.questionText: Why do many religions teach people to help those in need?
questions.explanation: Helping others expresses compassion and social responsibility.

questions.questionText: Which action best demonstrates forgiveness?

options.text: Choosing to stop seeking revenge after an apology

questions.explanation: Forgiveness involves letting go of the desire for revenge.

questions.questionText: Which is a Christian holy book?
questions.explanation: The Bible is the sacred text of Christianity.

questions.questionText: Which is the holy book of Islam?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is the central holy scripture of Islam.

questions.questionText: Why is prayer important to many believers?

options.text: It guarantees that no problems will occur
It is a form of farming
It provides a way to communicate with and worship God

questions.explanation: Prayer is a form of worship and spiritual communication.

questions.questionText: Which behaviour demonstrates respect for another person's beliefs?
questions.explanation: Respect means allowing others to hold and practise their beliefs peacefully.

questions.questionText: What is the moral lesson in returning a lost item to its owner?
questions.explanation: Returning lost property demonstrates honesty.

questions.questionText: Which action shows self-control?

options.text: Walking away from an argument before becoming violent

questions.explanation: Self-control helps a person manage strong emotions.

questions.questionText: Why are religious festivals often important to believers?

options.text: They are only for buying clothes
They provide opportunities for worship, remembrance and community

questions.explanation: Festivals often combine worship, remembrance and community activities.

questions.questionText: Which value is demonstrated when a learner admits making a mistake?
questions.explanation: Admitting a mistake is an honest and responsible action.

questions.questionText: What should a learner do after accidentally hurting a friend?

options.text: Apologise sincerely and try to make things right

questions.explanation: A sincere apology and corrective action can repair relationships.

questions.questionText: Which action best shows compassion?

options.text: Helping an injured classmate get assistance

questions.explanation: Compassion means recognising suffering and responding with care.

questions.questionText: Why is truthfulness important in examinations?

options.text: It guarantees every learner the highest mark
It removes the need to study

questions.explanation: Truthfulness supports fairness and trust in assessment.

questions.questionText: Which value helps people live peacefully despite differences?
questions.explanation: Tolerance allows people to coexist respectfully.

questions.questionText: Which practice is most effective for reducing the spread of germs?

options.text: Washing hands with soap and clean water

questions.explanation: Handwashing removes many germs and reduces transmission.

questions.questionText: Why should drinking water be kept in a clean, covered container?
questions.explanation: Covering and cleaning containers helps protect water from contamination.

questions.questionText: Which is a healthy personal hygiene practice?

options.text: Bathing regularly and wearing clean clothes

questions.explanation: Regular bathing and clean clothing support personal hygiene.

questions.questionText: What should a person do before preparing food?
questions.explanation: Clean hands reduce contamination of food.

questions.questionText: Which food-storage practice is safest?

options.text: Leave cooked food uncovered for days
Keep food covered and store perishable food appropriately

questions.explanation: Safe storage reduces contamination and spoilage.

questions.questionText: Why is a balanced diet important?

options.text: It removes the need for water
It supplies a variety of nutrients needed by the body
It means eating one food only

questions.explanation: A balanced diet provides different nutrients for growth and health.

questions.questionText: Which activity helps maintain physical fitness?
questions.explanation: Regular physical activity supports fitness.

questions.questionText: What is one safe action when a person gets a minor cut?

options.text: Clean it and protect it with a suitable dressing

questions.explanation: Cleaning and covering a minor wound helps prevent infection.

questions.questionText: Why should toilets be kept clean?

options.text: To reduce disease-causing germs and unpleasant conditions

questions.explanation: Clean sanitation facilities reduce health risks.

questions.questionText: Which habit helps protect teeth?
questions.explanation: Regular brushing helps remove plaque and protect teeth.

questions.questionText: What should a learner do if they feel seriously ill at school?

options.text: Tell a responsible adult and seek appropriate help

questions.explanation: Adults can help the learner obtain appropriate care.

questions.questionText: Why is adequate sleep important for children?

options.text: It supports growth, rest and concentration

questions.explanation: Sleep supports physical recovery, growth and mental functioning.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps prevent mosquito breeding near homes?

options.text: Keeping containers full of stagnant water

questions.explanation: Mosquitoes can breed in standing water.

questions.questionText: What is the safest response to an unknown medicine found at home?

options.text: Do not take it and tell a responsible adult

questions.explanation: Unknown medicines should not be taken without appropriate guidance.

questions.questionText: Why should food be protected from flies?

options.text: Flies can carry germs to food

questions.explanation: Flies can transfer harmful microorganisms and contaminants.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps conserve soil on sloping land?
questions.explanation: Terracing slows runoff and reduces soil erosion.

questions.questionText: What is recycling?

options.text: Processing used materials so they can be used again

questions.explanation: Recycling recovers materials for further use.

questions.questionText: Why are trees important to the environment?

options.text: They provide habitats, help protect soil and take in carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Trees provide ecological services including habitat and soil protection.

questions.questionText: Which action is most likely to pollute a river?
questions.explanation: Untreated waste can contaminate water.

questions.questionText: What is deforestation?
questions.explanation: Deforestation means removal or clearing of forests.

questions.questionText: Which practice can reduce household waste?
questions.explanation: Reuse reduces the amount of waste requiring disposal.

questions.questionText: Why should wetlands be protected?

options.text: They are useful only for dumping rubbish
They support biodiversity and help regulate water

questions.explanation: Wetlands provide habitats and important water-related functions.

questions.questionText: Which energy source is renewable?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is naturally replenished.

questions.questionText: What causes soil erosion most directly?

options.text: Removal of protective vegetation combined with wind or water action

questions.explanation: Bare soil is more vulnerable to erosion by wind and water.

questions.questionText: Which action helps conserve water at home?

options.text: Washing one item under running water for hours

questions.explanation: Fixing leaks reduces unnecessary water loss.

questions.questionText: Why should rubbish not be burned in enclosed spaces?

options.text: Smoke can pollute indoor air and harm health

questions.explanation: Smoke and harmful substances can accumulate in enclosed spaces.

questions.questionText: Which item is biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Organic fruit peel can decompose naturally.

questions.questionText: What is conservation?

options.text: Wise protection and management of natural resources

questions.explanation: Conservation means protecting and managing resources sustainably.

questions.questionText: Which practice can protect a riverbank from erosion?
questions.explanation: Vegetation helps hold soil and reduce runoff.

questions.questionText: Why should communities plant trees after cutting mature trees for approved uses?

options.text: To replace some of the lost vegetation

questions.explanation: Replanting supports continued vegetation cover and resource sustainability.

questions.questionText: Which soil property is especially important for healthy crop growth?
questions.explanation: Crops need nutrients, water and air around their roots.

questions.questionText: Why are seeds selected before planting?

options.text: To choose healthy, viable seeds likely to germinate well
To remove all water from soil

questions.explanation: Good seed selection improves establishment and crop performance.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps improve soil fertility using plant material?

options.text: Pouring used engine oil on the field

questions.explanation: Compost adds organic matter and nutrients.

questions.questionText: What is weeding?

options.text: Removing unwanted plants from a crop field

questions.explanation: Weeding removes plants that compete with crops.

questions.questionText: Why should farmers avoid overgrazing?

options.text: It can damage vegetation and increase soil erosion

questions.explanation: Overgrazing removes protective vegetation and can degrade land.

questions.questionText: Which animal product is commonly obtained from cattle?
questions.explanation: Cattle are commonly kept for milk, among other products.

questions.questionText: What is crop rotation?

options.text: Growing different crops on the same land in planned seasons

questions.explanation: Crop rotation changes crops across seasons to help manage soil and pests.

questions.questionText: Why is mulching useful around crops?

options.text: It can conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds

questions.explanation: Mulch can reduce evaporation and weed growth.

questions.questionText: Which is a good practice when storing harvested grain?

options.text: Store it in a wet place
Keep it dry and protected from pests

questions.explanation: Dry, protected storage reduces spoilage and pest damage.

questions.questionText: Which tool is commonly used to loosen soil by hand?
questions.explanation: A hoe is a common hand tool for cultivating soil.

questions.questionText: Why should farmers control crop pests?

options.text: Pests can reduce crop yield and quality

questions.explanation: Pests may damage plants and reduce production.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps reduce damage from water erosion on a field?

options.text: Making straight channels down a steep slope
Planting across the slope or using contours

questions.explanation: Contour-based practices can slow water movement.

questions.questionText: What is harvesting?

options.text: Collecting mature crops or useful plant parts

questions.explanation: Harvesting is the collection of mature agricultural produce.

questions.questionText: Why should farm tools be cleaned and stored properly?

options.text: It helps keep them usable and reduces damage

questions.explanation: Cleaning and proper storage extend tool life.

questions.questionText: Which practice helps protect young seedlings after planting?
questions.explanation: Appropriate water and weed control help seedlings establish.

questions.questionText: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.

questions.questionText: Which gas do humans need for normal respiration?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is required for aerobic respiration.

questions.questionText: What happens when water is heated to its boiling point under normal conditions?

options.text: It changes from liquid to gas

questions.explanation: Boiling changes liquid water into water vapour.

questions.questionText: Which force pulls objects toward the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity attracts objects toward Earth.

questions.questionText: Which simple machine is a seesaw an example of?
questions.explanation: A seesaw works as a lever.

questions.questionText: Which material is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Copper conducts electricity well.

questions.questionText: Why are insulators used around electrical wires?

options.text: To reduce the risk of electric shock

questions.explanation: Insulating materials help prevent current from reaching people.

questions.questionText: Which part of a plant absorbs most water and minerals from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and mineral nutrients.

questions.questionText: What is evaporation?

options.text: The change of solid into liquid only
The change of gas into solid
The change of a liquid into a gas at its surface

questions.explanation: Evaporation is a liquid-to-gas change at the surface.

questions.questionText: Which instrument measures temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.questionText: What is a habitat?

options.text: The place where an organism normally lives

questions.explanation: A habitat provides the conditions in which an organism lives.

questions.questionText: Which technology can help farmers receive weather information quickly?

options.text: A mobile phone or internet-enabled device

questions.explanation: Digital devices can provide access to weather information.

questions.questionText: Why should electrical appliances be kept away from water?

options.text: Water can increase the risk of electric shock

questions.explanation: Water can conduct electricity and increase shock risk.

questions.questionText: Which change is reversible?

options.text: Melting ice and freezing the water again

questions.explanation: Ice can melt and the water can freeze again.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of the lungs?
questions.explanation: The lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.questionText: Why should pedestrians use a designated crossing where one is available?

options.text: It helps them cross more safely
It guarantees no accidents can ever happen

questions.explanation: Designated crossings help organise safer pedestrian movement.

questions.questionText: What should a passenger do when travelling in a vehicle fitted with seat belts?
questions.explanation: Seat belts reduce injury risk during sudden stops or crashes.

questions.questionText: Why is speeding dangerous?

options.text: It reduces the time available to react and can increase crash severity

questions.explanation: Higher speed can reduce reaction time and increase collision energy.

questions.questionText: Which action is safest when approaching a road?

options.text: Stop, look carefully and cross when it is safe

questions.explanation: Careful observation and safe crossing reduce risk.

questions.questionText: What is one danger of driving after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol can impair judgement, coordination and reaction time.

questions.questionText: Which road user should be especially careful around a zebra crossing?
questions.explanation: Both drivers and pedestrians need to use crossings carefully.

questions.questionText: Why should bicycles be maintained properly?

options.text: It removes the need for road rules
Faulty brakes or tyres can cause accidents

questions.explanation: Safe brakes, tyres and other parts reduce mechanical risk.

questions.questionText: Which behaviour is unsafe on a moving bus?

options.text: Standing in a dangerous position or leaning outside

questions.explanation: Unsafe movement can cause falls or serious injury.

questions.questionText: What does a red traffic light normally mean for vehicles?
questions.explanation: A red light signals that vehicles should stop.

questions.questionText: Why should children avoid playing on roads?

options.text: Roads are used by moving vehicles and can be dangerous

questions.explanation: Moving traffic presents significant danger to children.

questions.questionText: Which emergency number should a person use?

options.text: A random number from an advert
An appropriate local emergency service number

questions.explanation: Emergency services should be contacted using the appropriate local number.

questions.questionText: What is the safest place to wait for a bus?

options.text: A designated or safe waiting area away from moving traffic

questions.explanation: Waiting away from traffic reduces the risk of being struck.

questions.questionText: Why are reflective materials useful at night?

options.text: They make a person more visible to drivers

questions.explanation: Reflective materials can improve visibility in low light.

questions.questionText: Which action helps reduce road accidents?

options.text: Following speed limits and traffic rules

questions.explanation: Following road rules reduces predictable risks.

questions.questionText: What should a learner do if they see a serious road accident?

options.text: Move to a safe place and alert an appropriate adult or emergency service

questions.explanation: Safety comes first, followed by getting appropriate assistance.

questions.questionText: Which element of art describes how light or dark something appears?
questions.explanation: Tone refers to lightness or darkness in visual art.

questions.questionText: What does tempo describe in music?
questions.explanation: Tempo is the speed at which music is performed.

questions.questionText: Which instrument belongs to the percussion family?
questions.explanation: A drum produces sound by being struck.

questions.questionText: Why is warming up important before vigorous exercise?

options.text: It removes the need for water
It prepares the body for activity and may reduce injury risk

questions.explanation: A suitable warm-up prepares muscles and the body for activity.

questions.questionText: Which quality is important in team sport?
questions.explanation: Teamwork requires cooperation.

questions.questionText: What is rhythm in music?

options.text: A pattern of beats or durations

questions.explanation: Rhythm is the organisation of beats and durations.

questions.questionText: Which activity is an example of visual art?
questions.explanation: Drawing is a visual art activity.

questions.questionText: Why should players follow the rules of a game?
questions.explanation: Rules establish fair and safe play.

questions.questionText: Which item can be used to make a simple musical shaker?

options.text: A sealed container with dry seeds
A broken glass bottle held loosely

questions.explanation: A safely sealed container with dry seeds can produce a shaking sound.

questions.questionText: What does fair play mean in sport?

options.text: Playing honestly and respecting opponents and officials

questions.explanation: Fair play involves honesty and respect.

questions.questionText: Which colour is made by mixing red and yellow paint?
questions.explanation: Red and yellow combine to make orange.

questions.questionText: Why should sports equipment be checked before use?

options.text: It removes the need for rules

questions.explanation: Checking equipment can identify hazards before play.

questions.questionText: Which body part is most directly used to kick a football?
questions.explanation: The foot is used to kick the ball.

questions.questionText: What is a sketch?

options.text: A quick drawing used to develop or communicate an idea

questions.explanation: A sketch is often a quick drawing used to explore an idea.

questions.questionText: Which quality is useful for an athlete during training?
questions.explanation: Discipline helps athletes train consistently and safely.

questions.questionText: What is citizenship?

options.text: Membership of a country with rights and responsibilities

questions.explanation: Citizenship involves belonging to a country and having rights and duties.

questions.questionText: Why are national symbols important?

options.text: They represent aspects of a nation's identity
They are only used for decoration

questions.explanation: National symbols represent national identity and values.

questions.questionText: Which is a responsibility of a good citizen?

options.text: Respecting laws and contributing positively to the community

questions.explanation: Responsible citizenship includes respecting laws and contributing to society.

questions.questionText: Why is voting important in a democratic society?

options.text: It allows eligible citizens to participate in choosing leaders

questions.explanation: Voting is a way for eligible citizens to participate in governance.

questions.questionText: Which institution is primarily associated with making national laws?
questions.explanation: Parliament is a key law-making institution.

questions.questionText: Why should public property be protected?

options.text: It serves the community and may be expensive to replace

questions.explanation: Public property is provided for community use.

questions.questionText: Which value supports peaceful citizenship?
questions.explanation: Respect supports peaceful relationships and responsible participation.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a national constitution?

options.text: It provides the fundamental framework for governance and rights

questions.explanation: A constitution establishes fundamental rules for governance and rights.

questions.questionText: Which action demonstrates responsible use of public resources?

options.text: Using facilities carefully and reporting damage

questions.explanation: Careful use protects resources for everyone.

questions.questionText: Why should historical records be preserved?

options.text: They provide evidence about the past

questions.explanation: Records help future generations understand past events.

questions.questionText: Which is an example of a human right?

options.text: The right to ignore every law

questions.explanation: Education is recognised as an important human right.

questions.questionText: Why is national unity important?

options.text: It requires everyone to have identical opinions
It helps people work together despite differences

questions.explanation: Unity helps citizens cooperate toward common goals.

questions.questionText: Which action shows respect for democratic discussion?

options.text: Listening to different views and responding peacefully

questions.explanation: Democratic discussion requires peaceful exchange and respect.

questions.questionText: What can a learner do to contribute positively to school life?

options.text: Follow rules, help others and care for school property

questions.explanation: Positive participation includes responsibility, care and cooperation.

questions.questionText: Why should citizens learn about national history?

options.text: It helps them understand how their society developed

questions.explanation: History helps citizens understand national development and identity.
